resources.string: Interoperability (experimental)
Roadstr can also read road reports written in the open jooray/roadstr format, published by other apps on Nostr.
Show compatible reports
Reports from other apps using the same open format. Their lifetime follows that format, not Roadstr\'s own.
Compatible report from the Nostr network (jooray/roadstr format)

Compatible report seen on Nostr and on MeshCore radio
Also publish in the compatible format

Each report is sent twice: Roadstr\'s own, and a copy other apps using the open jooray/roadstr format can read. Older Roadstr versions will show both markers. Your signer app may ask to approve the second event.
Sign the compatible copy with a one-time key
Not linked to your account and no second approval. Other Roadstr users will see two markers instead of one, because nobody can tell the copy is yours.
The compatible copy of your report could not be sent.
MeshCore — Experimental

Exchange road reports over a MeshCore LoRa radio, with or without internet. Anyone in radio range can read what is sent: position, time and the public key that signed it. It is neither private nor anonymous. A valid signature proves which key signed a report, not that the report is true. Not tested on real radios yet.
This device has no Bluetooth LE, so a MeshCore radio cannot be used.

Roadstr needs the “Nearby devices” permission to find a radio.
Transmit by radio?

What goes out on the radio can be received by anyone in range, with or without internet: the position of the report, its time and the public key that signed it (yours, or a one-time key if you chose that). It is not anonymous.

The bridges also pass other people's reports between the radio and the Nostr relays, always with their original author. A valid signature proves the key, not that the report is true.

You can switch every radio feature off at any time, and clear what is waiting to be published.
